notes: DOE Office of Energy Dominance Financing closed a loan of up to $1.9B to NextEra Energy to restart the 615MW Duane Arnold plant (Linn County, IA), shuttered since 2020, targeting Q1 2029 restart. Second DOE loan of this kind after the ~$1B Constellation/Three Mile Island loan. Underpinned by a 25-year PPA with Google, which will take the power for cloud/AI infrastructure -- Google is the demand anchor but is not itself party to the loan (US Government is the allocator here, not Google). Corroborated by NextEra Energy's own press release (newsroom.nexteraenergy.com, same date) and wide press pickup (Reuters/TechCrunch/Engadget/Iowa Public Radio, all 2026-09-08/09).

Dept of Commerce (CHIPS R&D Office) finalized a CHIPS Act award of up to $375M to GlobalFoundries over 5 years, milestone-gated, to build a secure domestic quantum foundry (cryogenic CMOS PDKs, advanced packaging). Distinct from GlobalFoundries' separate $300M silicon-photonics LOI announced 2026-07-29 (already on file, id 89/194/213) -- different program, different amount, do not merge. Confirmed independently by GlobalFoundries' own release (gf.com, same date).

Dept of Commerce finalized a CHIPS Act award of up to $100M to Rigetti for superconducting quantum computing R&D (readout electronics, cryostats, fab capability): $43.9M disbursed at signing, $29.9M and $26.2M tranches milestone-gated. Same-day, the government also received 7,739,938 Rigetti common shares (~$100M notional at $12.92/share implied price) as a non-controlling equity kicker -- same Intel-style CHIPS equity structure. Filed as a single grant row (not a separate equity row) to avoid double-counting the same $100M pool. Confirmed by Rigetti's own 8-K exhibit (SEC EDGAR, cited) and NIST/Commerce release (nist.gov, same date).
